stage: R14 Phase 2 diagnostics (no training): ordering/amplitude decomposition of the shape term
identity: shape = Var(y)(1-r^2) + (sd_p - r*sd_y)^2, exact; the first term is the ordering floor, the second is removable by a positive rescale that cannot change any rank metric

G1.training: shape-first on the incumbent trunk (zero architecture change)

findings.claim: every ranking-primary / shape-first arm has a worse k=0 ordering floor than the plain MSE-trained incumbent
findings.evidence: 8 of 8 arms; A0 ordering floor 0.6922 is the minimum over the whole project

findings.claim: the loss of within-target ordering is caused by the training method, not the architecture
findings.evidence: G1 is the incumbent architecture with zero changes trained by the shape-first method: k=0 Pearson r falls 0.213 -> 0.134 (-37%)

findings.claim: the retained 'shape-first is the project's first within-target shape source' claim is causally wrong at k=0; it is an amplitude-suppression source
findings.evidence: B1 vs A0: ordering floor +0.043 WORSE (0.735 vs 0.692), amplitude excess -0.060, net shape -0.017
findings.record_action: corrected in report/CURRENT_MODEL_EVIDENCE.md, report/BOUNDARY_20260816.md, task.md, history.md

findings.claim: a single global amplitude rescale is not a usable lever
findings.evidence: leave-one-component-out rescale makes k=0 MSE worse for 6 of 8 arms; the two gains (D1, D2) are <=0.023 and occur only in the most collapsed arms

findings.claim: a protein-conditioned amplitude head is not supported and is dropped before implementation
findings.evidence: the per-target oracle rescale is worth 0.221 MSE (2.1488 -> 1.9280) but the optimal scale has IQR [0.02, 5.36], is NEGATIVE in 25.2% of targets (an ordering fix, not an amplitude one), and is numerically unstable wherever sd_p is small (C2 seed-transfer diverges to 29.8)

findings.claim: k=0 within-target Pearson r is the only quantity that improves MSE and CI together
findings.evidence: at the MSE-optimal amplitude shape equals the ordering floor exactly, so achievable MSE = calibration + Var(y)(1-r^2) with Var(y) ~ 0.725

findings.claim: the regression-compatible ListCE contributes exactly zero gradient at the regression optimum, while RankNet and hinge do not
findings.evidence: 200 synthetic 16-query panels: max gradient norm at s=y is 1.7e-17 for ListCE, 1.02e-01 for RankNet, 7.36e-02 for hinge; ListCE is also stationary at any positive multiple of the centered label (3.9e-18 at scale 1.7)
findings.consequence: names the mechanism behind F1/F2 — the incumbent ranking losses pull away from s=y even when the prediction is already correct — and clears the R14 design's first listed failure mode

findings.claim: support observations do supply within-target ordering; the deficit is specific to k=0
findings.evidence: A0 r rises 0.213 -> 0.348 from k=0 to k=5; at k=5 the ordering floors converge across arms and G1 slightly beats A0 (0.631 vs 0.646)

headroom_at_A0_calibration.note: k=0 MSE = 1.2358 + 0.725*(1-r^2), i.e. at the per-target optimal amplitude

design_consequence: one core innovation survives Phase 2 and it is a training innovation: a ranking term whose optimum coincides with the regression optimum, so it cannot trade r away for coarse rank statistics. The model-side candidate (protein-conditioned amplitude) is dropped, not replaced.
